sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The goddess-king marriage names the union of the land goddess and the king. See SOVEREIGNTY for the full entry. In Celtic Ireland the land goddess wed the king at his inauguration. The figure of Sovereignty varies. She can be the loathy Hag who gives Niall a drink. She can be Ériu, the land's titular goddess. She can be Medb, who weds king after king. The king must keep the land fertile through righteous rule. He must offer hospitality and honor sacred taboos.
